title: Honest Interval Width for Missing-Not-at-Random Categorical Means with Near-Singular Shadow Variables
banked_reason: D-0.5 reviewer retained field-tier potential and cleared soundness/structure but required a theorem-level Nakano--Hoshino comparison before Stage 0; only its abstract and author README were accessible, and the supervisor one-round cap ended this run.
gap_reasons: NakanoHoshino2026 is a close MNAR weak-identification comparator, but only its abstract is inspectable; its theorem text and assumptions have not been compared against the central matching-diameter claim.
Keep the fixed-cell theorem at field potential, but require a theorem-level Nakano--Hoshino comparison before advancing to Stage 0.
proof_attempt_summary: Six D-0.5 reviews refined the finite weak-shadow inference proposal. The final draft repaired the full-data versus observed-law notation and the coincident-column atlas endpoint; the reviewer reported field-tier potential with no soundness or structure flags. Stage 0 derivation and Lean formalization were not attempted because the reviewer required theorem-level comparison with Nakano--Hoshino (2026), whose manuscript remained inaccessible despite an abstract and author-repository comparison; the supervisor's one-round cap ended the run.
tldr: Can the width of a uniformly honest interval for a selectively missing categorical mean be characterized by an observable residual fiber as the estimated shadow operator loses rank or the feasible face changes? The fixed finite positive-recorded-cell proposal seeks matching law-specific expected-diameter bounds for one two-LP interval and an exact three-outcome atlas. A randomized full potential-outcomes extension gives a point-identified contrast with nonunique arm fibers and poses a separate observable-law transport-modulus question. The Nakano–Hoshino novelty comparison is bounded by its accessible abstract and author README; theorem-level noncollision is unverified.
gap: Sharp weak-shadow bounds and fixed-law inference are available, while the inspected categorical and general linear-system theorem text does not state the proposed every-law matching expected-diameter result. Nakano–Hoshino is a direct affine-shadow weak-relevance neighbor: its abstract and author README support only a source-bounded comparison, and theorem-level noncollision is unverified because the manuscript and theorem/hypothesis text are inaccessible.
fill: Prove the fixed-cell residual-modulus equivalence and exact phase atlas, give a valid randomized potential-outcomes contrast example, and investigate a joint observable-law transport modulus for sampled target weights.
